name: Hexomatic
tagline: Cloud scraping, monitoring, and automation with prebuilt actions

pricing.native: Usage or capacity pricing; exact monthly cost varies
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Silver
tiers.limits: 4,500 automation credits/month; 10 simultaneous running workflows; unlimited custom scraping recipes and scheduled workflows

tiers.name: Gold
tiers.limits: 10,000 automation credits/month; unlimited simultaneous workflows; residential-proxy access through premium credits

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom credits, onboarding, team training, campaign management, scraping templates, automations and strategy support

pricing.billingTerms: monthly or annual paid plans; annual is equivalent to 2 months free; 7-day trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Automation credits renew monthly; premium features such as ChatGPT, translation, Google/Maps data, email enrichment, residential proxies, Amazon data and backlink data require a premium-credit add-on starting at $9.99/month; Hexomatic Second Brain is a separate subscription

verdictSummary: The visible web scraping + automation loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Hexomatic earns its keep through connectors, auth, reliability, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build one explicit web scraping + automation workflow with a trigger, validated steps, retries, logs, and a manual replay button.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: API credentials for the two chosen services
whatYouLose: schema drift handling and enterprise controls
whyPeopleStillPay: Hexomatic: One automation is easy. Subscribers pay for maintained integrations, credentials, retries, observability, and someone else owning breakage.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, rate limits, webhooks, retries, queues, idempotency, logs, secret rotation, and third-party API changes.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Hexomatic is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Hexomatic, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build one explicit web scraping + automation workflow with a trigger, validated steps, retries, logs, and a manual replay button.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: durable execution at scale; schema drift handling and enterprise controls; hundreds of maintained connectors.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
